lens: Numerical analysis / approximation theory. The object to be learned is a point on the SPD cone with the structure of a discrete Dirichlet-to-Neumann (Steklov-Poincare) map of a *local* elliptic operator (CutFEM elasticity with ghost penalty). The correct geometry on that cone for this deliverable is the Thompson (Loewner-sandwich) metric d_T(A,Ahat) = max(log mu_max, -log mu_min): it is exactly the acceptance statistic eps_op in log form, it is the sharp worst-case first-order relative compliance error over all loads, and every operation in the pipeline (congruence/quotient, assembly sums, Schur complements, inversion) is non-expansive in it, while every additive/entrywise operation (regression of entries, Frobenius truncation, banding) is expansive by up to cond(A). Approximation classes are judged by their error in this metric; learnability is judged by the regularity of geometry -> S in this metric, which is compositional (smooth low-dimensional local pieces + exact global algebra), not global.
principles: P1 (metric): eps_op = max|mu-1| is the sup over loads of the first-order relative compliance error and equals the Loewner-sandwich constant; it composes exactly under assembly and condensation (Thompson metric non-expansiveness), so the module certificate is the lattice certificate for any load, any lattice. Averaged statistics (D/d, Frobenius, action-MSE) only bound eps_op by sqrt(2 d L) and cannot certify anything.

P2 (amplification): additive errors on A are amplified by cond(A) = 7.2e4 at worst, additive errors on the factor by sqrt(cond) = 269, left-multiplicative factor errors (I+Delta)R* by nothing; per-element relative (Loewner) errors are also amplified by nothing because Schur complements and sums are monotone and homogeneous. Parameterise every learned SPD object multiplicatively (positive weights, scales, tensors), never by entries.

P3 (cancellation): the deciding soft modes are near/far cancellations with Jacobi ratio rho_J = w^T diag(A) w / w^T A w ~ 1e3-1e4. Independent entry-relative factor noise eps gives eps_op ~ 2 eps sqrt(rho_J) (~111 eps, matching the measured 1.11e-2 at 1e-4); a systematic near-vs-far relative bias delta gives eps_op ~ delta rho_J, so any representation that predicts near and far field independently must keep them coherent to 3e-6..3e-5. Only representations that generate the far field from an interior solve get the cancellation for free.

P4 (classes): a DtN map is nonlocal with algebraic kernel decay (~|x-y|^-3 on the surface; its factor ~|x-y|^-2, log-divergent energy). Banded factors and sparse multiscale factors (T^T D T with block-diagonal D, Vecchia/screening-type sparsity) converge algebraically or not at all; hierarchical low rank converges log-linearly (passes +-3% at ~15% of dense, near field ~7%); locality is recovered only by keeping an interior (collar + core), where high-frequency trace data decays exponentially with depth.

P5 (loss): to control max|mu-1| the loss must dominate it (sup-type or Schatten-2k moment, two-sided in mu and 1/mu) with the extreme modes tracked by warm-started block Lanczos on the whitened pencil; cost ~100 operator applies + triangular solves per step, an audit eigendecomposition per epoch. A Loewner log-barrier with an epsilon homotopy is the principled interior-point form.

P6 (gauge): the loss must be a function of Ahat's action only; regression targets must be gauge-free and continuous in the operator: Cholesky in a fixed background-grid ordering (Lipschitz in the whitened metric with constant ~log d), fixed-probe sketches B*Omega (linear in B), fixed-skeleton CUR sub-blocks, element matrices in the fixed local basis. SVD factors, (T,D) pairs and any auxiliary matrices are not labels.

P7 (teacher regularity): A(theta) = sum_e sum_alpha m_alpha^e(theta) G_alpha + gamma sum_{F in GP(theta)} J_F is piecewise real-analytic in the cut-region moments with jump discontinuities from the discrete GP face set; the jumps are O(1) on the softest modes (59.8% from a 5.6e-15 cell) and invisible to end-load compliance. No continuous predictor can meet +-3% against this teacher near an event, and events are dense at the resolution of any training set.

P8 (sample complexity): 33 seats x 48 symmetries or 1024 packets x 48 give ~3 points per axis of a 9-D geometry space; global smoothness cannot carry generalisation at 1e-4 coherence. Exact weight sharing holds only for objects that are local functions of geometry (element matrices, GP faces, local upscaled tensors) and gives 1e5-1e7 samples of a ~6-8 dimensional smooth map; entries of S or R* are global functions and weight sharing on them is biased exactly in the deciding modes.

P9 (target): the mathematically cleanest regression target is the set of local SPD contributions in a fixed local basis (cut-cell moments / element matrices, GP face set, local core tensors), with the global coupling computed by exact algebra on a reduced interior; the per-element relative tolerance then equals the gate (3%), not 1e-4, and the Galerkin core gives a structural one-sided bound Shat >= S.

P10 (certificate): report d_T (equivalently eps_op with the count of modes outside the gate) per module on teacher seats, optionally in a registered shifted metric (A+E) that excludes GP-dominated modes below a physically validated floor; add a derivative certificate via uniform sandwich over a theta-ball; for new geometries only structural one-sided bounds or hypercircle-type a posteriori bounds are teacher-free.
implications_for_representation: Classify representations by their behaviour under the Thompson metric and the near/far cancellation. (i) Banded: provably hopeless for any radius because the factor's far field has log-divergent energy along smooth soft modes; the measured radius-independent mu_max 59-144 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED] is the factor-level cancellation ratio (~sqrt of the A-level 1e3-1e4). (ii) Sparse multiscale factors T^T D T with block-diagonal D are wavelet-diagonal preconditioners: spectrally equivalent with O(1) constants, never +-3%; the Vecchia/screening exponential theory (Schaefer et al.) does not apply to boundary-restricted operators, so their convergence is algebraic; abandon block-diagonal D. (iii) Low-rank-plus-sparse fails because the off-band part of a DtN has rank ~N^(1/2)*log and because a one-sided softening term cannot fix a wrong band (reachability criterion). (iv) H/H^2 low rank is the right *storage* class (log-linear; ~15% of dense at +-3%, R* 1.17x cheaper than A); a learnable version needs a fixed cluster tree on the background superset, fixed ranks per level, and gauge-free factor data (fixed-probe sketches / fixed skeletons), with accuracy demands that are rank-dependent: the leading smooth components of far-field blocks must be coherent with the near field to ~1e-5 relative, the tails can be loose. (v) Schur-structured representations (collar + reduced core, or fine element matrices + reduced interior) are the only class in which the cancellation is generated rather than stored, in which per-parameter relative error maps 1:1 to eps_op, and in which the teacher's GP-event discontinuity is produced by exact algebra from a local switch; their floor is the Kolmogorov n-width of A-harmonic extensions restricted to the core (thin-sheet bending needs shell-like or spectrally enriched core kinematics; the Q1 core's Loewner floor 1.111 is locking). Approximating S^-1 instead of S changes which modes cancel (stiff instead of soft) but not the whitened requirement; the metric is inversion-symmetric.
implications_for_loss_and_metric: Use d_T / eps_op as the headline and as the optimisation target. Bulk term: whitened divergence or sum (log mu_i)^2 (gradient weight proportional to the error, well conditioned). Tail term: two-sided soft-max (log-sum-exp) over the k worst Ritz values of the whitened pencil at both ends, or a Schatten-2k moment tr((M-I)^{2k})^{1/2k} which is a certified upper bound within d^{1/2k} (1.34 for 2k=32) estimated by Hutchinson probes; or a Loewner log-barrier -sum[log(1+eps-mu_i)+log(mu_i-1+eps)] with an eps homotopy (interior-point path following). Never use a one-sided extreme term (the mu_max 15->5, mu_min 0.13->0.05 outcome [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] is the expected whack-a-mole of a one-sided sup loss on a capacity-limited class). The loss must depend on Ahat only (gauge invariance kills the auxiliary-matrix drift). Whitening: on seats, whiten exactly with R*^-1 (two dense triangular solves per apply, ~1e8 flops); at inference time the best available whitening is the predicted column compliance scale (R^2 0.98, curvature spread 1e4 -> 17), so parameterise outputs relative to that scale. Cheap tracking of max|mu-1|: warm-started block Lanczos/LOBPCG (8-32 vectors, 2-5 iterations per step, full restart every ~100 steps), fixed soft-eigenvector probes of the teacher (precomputed per seat) as a lower bound, exact eigendecomposition per epoch as audit. Report always: eps_op, number of modes outside +-3% and +-10%, and the soft-subspace projection of the residual. Factor all 1024 S packets on GPU (d^3/3 flops, seconds to a minute each) so the whitened loss is available on all of them.
implications_for_data_and_teacher: The teacher is piecewise analytic in the cut-region moments with jumps from the discrete ghost-penalty face set that are O(1) on the deciding modes [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY OF THE TEACHER]; between events the whitened Lipschitz constant is O(1-3) per unit relative thickness (bending ~t^3), and the cross-seat eps_op 536-3847 reflects order-of-magnitude differences in local thickness of thin regions, not intrinsic roughness. Consequences: (a) regenerate labels with a continuous stabilisation (aggregation/ghost weights that are smooth functions of the cut fraction, tending to a hard constraint as the fraction -> 0 and to zero as it -> 1) so S(theta) becomes continuous and piecewise analytic; the 1e-12 threshold sensitivity of the hard classifier is removed by construction; (b) alternatively register a spectral floor: certify in the shifted metric (A+E, Ahat+E) with a local PSD E at the scale where GP bridging dominates physics; this composes under assembly (it is a known added regularising stiffness) and is honest because the Tet10 validation never probed those modes; (c) always feed active-set features (cell volume fractions, GP face indicators, node masks) as exact inputs, but note they only help local representations. Data: symmetry gives 48x exact augmentation; 33 factors + 1024 packets is ~3 points per geometry axis, useless for global interpolation at 1e-4 but ample for local maps (2.5e5 cut cells, 3.6e4 coarse cells, each a sample of a ~6-8 dimensional smooth map). Factor the 1024 packets to obtain whitened labels for all of them. Learn or compute in log-thickness-type coordinates (multiplicative outputs).
implications_for_architecture: Architecture must mirror the operator's structure: local smooth pieces predicted (or computed) with spatial weight sharing and cube-group equivariance, global coupling produced by exact linear algebra. Tier A (recommended): exact cut-cell moments (Q2 element matrices are linear in 125 monomial moments of cell∩Omega; GP face matrices are constant on a geometry-dependent set) + a reduced interior (one fine collar layer + a core with shell-like or spectrally enriched kinematics, or a GenEO/MsFEM-type locally computed basis) + exact condensation of the reduced problem (~1e4-6e4 dofs, seconds). Learning enters only where a local computation is too slow or where the core enrichment must be chosen: local networks predicting positive quadrature weights or local SPD tensors (multiplicative parameterisation), whose relative error maps 1:1 to eps_op. Tier B (if no interior solve is allowed): an H^2/FMM-shaped network on a fixed background cluster tree, outputs = gauge-free block data (dense near-field blocks + fixed-probe sketches of admissible blocks), trained on the action with the whitened bulk+tail loss; expect the +-10% work gate on the bulk to be reachable and the soft modes not, because near/far coherence at 3e-6..3e-5 must be learned from ~1e3 geometries. Tier C: Tier B used as a preconditioner (mode B) needs only d_T <~ log 1.3, but each lattice solve then needs the true S action (fine interior solves), which roughly cancels the saving. Avoid: entry-regressed dense factors, SVD coefficients as targets, one-sided low-rank corrections, block-diagonal D, any parameterisation with a nontrivial gauge group, receptive fields smaller than the cell when the output is a global object.
hard_constraints: The acceptance metric composes exactly: (1-eps)S_c <= Shat_c <= (1+eps)S_c for every cell implies the same sandwich for any assembled lattice, and eps is the sharp worst-case first-order relative compliance error; the measured 0.31% compliance error at eps_op 0.152 [ASSEMBLY / DELIVERABLE] is a favourable alignment, not a law.

Any averaged loss L (D/d, Frobenius, action-MSE, whitened Frobenius) bounds max|mu-1| only by ~sqrt(2 d L): at d = 12,792, L = 1.27e-5 permits eps_op up to 0.57 [METRIC]; certification requires a sup-type statistic.

Additive error on A is amplified by up to cond(A) = 7.2e4; additive error on R* by up to sqrt(cond) = 269; left-multiplicative factor error and per-element Loewner-relative error are not amplified at all [METRIC].

Independent entry-relative noise eps on the factor gives eps_op ~ 2 eps sqrt(rho_J) with rho_J the Jacobi cancellation ratio (1e3-1e4): 1e-4 -> ~1e-2 [ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS]; a relative near-vs-far bias delta gives eps_op ~ delta rho_J, i.e. 3e-6..3e-5 coherence for +-3%; a uniform relative scaling is harmless.

Banded truncation of the factor fails at every radius (mu_max 59-144, ~300 damaged modes) because the factor's far field has log-divergent energy along smooth soft modes [STRUCTURE OF S]; no spatial cut-off can pass.

Block-diagonal D in T^T D T is a wavelet-diagonal preconditioner: closed-form oracle 63-204x above the +-10% line; no fitting of T repairs it at comparable budgets (eps_op 15.2 at 7.4M params vs H-matrix pass at 12.2M) [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED].

The GP teacher is discontinuous in geometry: a +0.01% thickness change stiffens one 1.1e-6 direction by 59.8% via 3 new GP faces on a 5.6e-15 volume-fraction cell; operator central differences are unstable (87%), task-level derivatives are stable (0.023%) [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY OF THE TEACHER]. A continuous predictor cannot meet +-3% against this teacher in a neighbourhood of an event.

Any fixed-collar + Q1 core representation has a Loewner floor mu_max >= 1.111 (locking); a Galerkin core always gives Shat >= S; passing needs richer core kinematics, a deeper collar, or spectral enrichment [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED].

SVD factors, (T,D) pairs and low-rank M/U auxiliaries have nontrivial gauge groups; coefficient regression on them is ill-posed and the loss must be a function of the operator only (the 2.5x auxiliary-gauge distortion is a symptom) [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED].

Cross-seat operators differ by eps_op 536-3847 at geometric distance 0.14-0.36; with 33 (or 1024) x 48 samples in ~9 geometry dimensions, no zero-shot transplant and no global interpolation can reach 1e-4 coherence; only local/compositional structure can generalise [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY OF THE TEACHER].
open_questions: Which residual model a trained network actually produces: independent, block-coherent, or near/far-biased? Decisive oracle test with existing tools: take the passing H-matrix of R* and perturb near-field and far-field blocks by independent smooth relative fields (1e-3, 1e-4); if eps_op fails by >10x the global-regression route is dead before training.

Are the softest ~188 teacher modes physically right at O(1)? GP bridging contributes O(gamma) stiffness where physics gives ~1e-6; the Tet10 validation only probed end-load compliance. This decides whether a registered spectral floor (shifted metric) is the honest contract.

What is the Kolmogorov n-width of the A-harmonic extension restricted to the core (one-collar-layer oversampling) on a thin-sheet cell? Computable on one seat with the fine factor (transfer eigenproblem); it sets the minimal core dimension for +-3% and whether Q2/shell/GenEO enrichment suffices.

Can a continuous-weight aggregation (soft AgFEM / cut-fraction-weighted ghost penalty) be implemented in the frozen teacher pipeline, and what is the resulting whitened Lipschitz constant of geometry -> S along thickness paths?

How fast can exact cut-cell moment quadrature run on GPU for 7,478 cells (linear reconstruction of Q2 element matrices from 125 moments)? If seconds, the element level needs no learning at all and the whole cost is the reduced condensation.

For Tier B, does an equivariant H^2/FMM-shaped network trained with the whitened bulk+tail loss on 1024 factored packets reach the +-10% work gate on the bulk, and how many modes remain outside? (No such experiment exists; V1 used a representation class that provably could not pass.)
Deployment: is an inference-time reduced interior solve of ~1-3 s per cell acceptable? If not, only Tier B/C remain and the analysis predicts they do not deliver a +-3% certificate on the soft modes.

Derivative contract for TO: uniform sandwich over a theta-ball gives |d Shat - d S| <~ 2 eps ||S||/h in the whitened norm; is a task-level (compliance/sensitivity) derivative certificate with registered load scope acceptable instead of an operator-derivative one?

Does a Tier-A model with exact element matrices and a learned/computed core enrichment beat 31.85 s on the same hardware once the collar assembly (17.7 s) is replaced by moment quadrature and the pre-elimination is done on the reduced system?

# Representing and learning geometry -> S: a numerical-analysis / approximation-theory account

All numbers cited by tag are from the project's measurements (2026-09-11 to 09-16) and are treated as constraints. d = 12,792 (seat 0328), lam_min(A) = 4.9e-7, lam_max = 3.5e-2, cond(A) = 7.2e4 [METRIC].

## 0. The lens in one paragraph

S is the discrete Dirichlet-to-Neumann (Steklov-Poincare) map of a *local* operator: the CutFEM elasticity stiffness A_full(theta) on 231k dofs, whose Schur complement onto the trace is S. Everything that is hard about S comes from that: the interior has been integrated out, so S is dense with algebraically decaying kernel, and its softest eigen-directions (thin-material bending, stiffness ~1e-6 of the mean) are differences of a large *near-field* energy and an almost equal *far-field* energy generated by the interior response [STRUCTURE OF S]. The right way to measure errors is the Thompson (part) metric on the SPD cone, d_T(A, Ahat) = max(log mu_max, -log mu_min), which is exactly the Loewner sandwich e^{-d}A <= Ahat <= e^{d}A and equals log(1+eps_op) to first order. The core facts below are all consequences of three properties of d_T: it is non-expansive under congruence, under sums (assembly), under Schur complements (condensation) and under inversion, and it is expansive by up to cond(A) under additive/entrywise operations.

## 1. Approximation classes for S and for its factor

### 1.1 What kind of operator S is

For a smooth elastic body the continuum DtN map is a classical pseudodifferential operator of order +1; its Schwartz kernel is asymptotically smooth off the diagonal and decays like |x-y|^{-3} on the 2-D boundary (the hypersingular kernel of the Green's function). Its inverse, the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map S^{-1} = (A_full^{-1})_{Gamma Gamma}, is of order -1 with kernel ~ |x-y|^{-1}: a boundary restriction of a Green's matrix. A Cholesky factor of S behaves like a "half-order" object with kernel ~ |x-y|^{-2}. Three consequences:

* **Entry decay is algebraic, not exponential.** Along a smooth test vector w (constant sign over the far field), the far-field energy of S beyond radius r on a surface scales like integral_r^1 rho^{-3} rho d rho ~ 1/r, and for the factor like integral_r^1 rho^{-2} rho d rho ~ log(1/r): the factor's far-field energy is *log-divergent*, so any band radius removes an O(1) fraction (in log measure) of the far field. That is the analytic reason the banded factor fails at every radius with mu_max nearly independent of radius (59-144 at radius 0.25 and at every other radius, ~300 damaged modes) [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (c), STRUCTURE OF S].
* **Admissible blocks are numerically low rank** with epsilon-rank growing polylogarithmically in 1/epsilon (degenerate-kernel/Taylor expansions; Hackbusch, Bebendorf). Confirmed: none of 2965 admissible blocks hit the rank cap, top-8 singular values carry >= 99.5% of far-field face-face block energy [STRUCTURE OF S].
* **The soft modes are cancellations.** For a soft eigenvector w, w^T A w = lam_soft while the diagonal (near-field) energy w^T diag(A) w is 1e3-1e4 times larger; define the Jacobi cancellation ratio rho_J(w) = w^T diag(A) w / w^T A w <= 1/lam_min(D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}). This single number governs sections 1, 2 and 4.

### 1.2 The classes, with their theoretical rates and what the measurements confirm

**Dense.** Exact; 8.2e7 numbers for the factor; the reference against which everything is measured.

**Banded / spatially truncated (S or R*).** Provably fails in the Thompson metric for any radius: truncating the far field of the factor changes the stiffness of the soft mode w from lam_soft to ~||R*_band w||^2, i.e. by the factor-level cancellation ratio rho_R(w). The measured mu_max 59-144 is that ratio; it is ~sqrt of the A-level ratio 1e3-1e4, consistent with the factor being a half-order object. No refinement of banding (variable bandwidth, ordering) changes this: the damaged directions are the physical thin-material modes [STRUCTURE OF S], which are global.

**Hierarchical low rank (H, H^2, HSS).** For a 2-D boundary the H-matrix storage is O(N log N r(eps)) with r polylogarithmic; H^2 removes a log factor by nesting; HSS (weak admissibility) has top-level ranks ~N^{1/2} log(1/eps) for 2-D boundaries, so O(N^{1.5}) storage, comparable at N = 1.3e4. Butterfly compression addresses oscillatory kernels and gives nothing here (static elasticity). Measured: R* in H-format (leaf 64, eta = 2) passes +-3% at 12.23M numbers = 14.95% of dense; on four seats 13.9-15.6% for +-3%, 11.8-13.6% for +-10%; approximating A instead costs 1.17x more [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (a)]. The accounting: the 1344 near-field 64x64 blocks alone are ~5.5M numbers (~7% of dense), so far-field ranks average ~18 per admissible block, i.e. polylog ranks at ~1e-3-type block tolerances. The class is right for *storage*; theoretical levers (H^2 nesting, eta = 1, larger leaves) buy at most a factor ~1.5-2, not an order of magnitude. Two facts matter for learning: (i) ranks were adaptive per block; a learnable version needs fixed ranks per level (max over geometries plus margin), (ii) SVD truncation residuals are high-frequency (the tail singular vectors) and therefore *weakly aligned with the smooth soft modes*; that is why blockwise tolerances of ~1e-3 on A produce eps_op 0.23 rather than the worst-case 70. A network's residual has no reason to be so benign (section 4).

**Low-rank plus sparse (banded L + global rank-k M, one-sided).** Fails for two independent reasons. Structurally, the off-band part of a DtN on a 2-D boundary has rank ~N^{1/2} log (a separator argument), i.e. thousands, not 512. Algebraically, a softening term (I+MM^T)^{-1} can only lower stiffness, so the fixed band must already satisfy lam_min(H0) >= 1-tau; measured 0.02-0.13 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (c)]. Adding a hardening term restores two-sidedness but not the rank deficit, and the unconstrained auxiliary matrix added a gauge drift that distorted the loss 2.5x.

**Factored T^T D T (multiscale unit-triangular lifting + block-diagonal D).** With T a fixed multiscale change of basis this is a *wavelet-diagonal* approximation of an order-1 operator: the classical result (Beylkin-Coifman-Rokhlin; Dahmen-Schneider) is that such operators are *quasi-sparse* in a wavelet basis with O(N log N) significant coefficients above a tolerance, and that dropping the off-diagonal coefficients yields *spectral equivalence* (a preconditioner with O(1) condition number), never +-3%. The measured closed-form oracle floor 63-204x above the +-10% line and eps_op 15.2 after fitting T at 7.4M parameters [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (d)] are exactly that. To become accurate, D must acquire the wavelet-sparse fill, at which point it is an H-matrix in a worse basis. A second theoretical warning: the exponential-accuracy theory for sparse Cholesky factors under maximin orderings (Schaefer-Sullivan-Owhadi 2021; Schaefer-Katzfuss-Owhadi 2021, whose KL objective is exactly the project's divergence D) requires a Green's matrix of a *local* operator sampled throughout the domain (the screening effect). S^{-1} is the boundary restriction of such a matrix and S is its precision; the trace of a Markov field is not Markov, screening is only algebraic on a submanifold, and the sparse-factor convergence is algebraic. Sparse multiscale factors of S or S^{-1} are therefore not competitive with H-matrices, matching the measurement.

**Collar + reduced core (Schur-structured).** Keep one layer of fine cut cells and replace the deep interior by a reduced Galerkin space V_c; Shat = Schur complement over (trace + collar + V_c). Three exact properties: Shat >= S always (minimising energy over a subspace); the SPD structure and rigid nullspace are exact by construction; and the far field is *generated* by the reduced interior solve, so near/far cancellation is automatic to the accuracy of V_c. The floor is a Kolmogorov n-width: mu_max - 1 = sup_g [min_{V_c} E(g,.) - min E(g,.)]/min E(g,.), the worst relative energy excess of A-harmonic extensions restricted to V_c. The theory of optimal local approximation spaces (Babuska-Lipton 2011; Ma-Scheichl-Dodwell 2022) gives nearly exponential decay exp(-c n^{1/4}) in the space dimension n with c set by the oversampling ratio; here the oversampling is one collar layer (h = 1/32), so c is small and V_c must be large or well adapted. High-frequency trace data decays into the interior like exp(-k delta), but for a thin sheet the relevant decay length along the sheet is the sheet thickness, not h, so a one-layer collar leaves O(1) residuals at the core interface unless the core can bend. That is the analytic content of the Loewner floor mu_max >= 1.111 for a fixed collar with a Q1 core (locking) [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (e)]: not a failure of the class, a failure of Q1 kinematics. Remedies: Q2 or shell-like core kinematics, a two-layer collar, or spectral enrichment of the core (GenEO / GMsFEM-type local eigenmodes, which come with Loewner-type energy bounds).

### 1.3 Where the classes stand in the metric

The classification is: representations that discard the interior pay either polylog ranks (H, passes at ~15%) or algebraic sparsity decay (banded, T^T D T, hopeless); representations that keep an interior, even a coarse one, regain locality and can be certified structurally. This is not a preference; it is where the nonlocality of a DtN map goes when the interior is eliminated.

## 2. The right error metric and its consequences

### 2.1 The metric

M = R*^{-T} Ahat R*^{-1}, mu = eig(M) = eig of the pencil (Ahat, A); eps_op = max|mu-1| iff (1-eps_op) A <= Ahat <= (1+eps_op) A. Properties:

* **Sharpness for compliance.** For any load f with response u, the first-order relative compliance error is dC/C = -u^T (Ahat - A) u / u^T A u in [-eps_op, eps_op], with equality attained by the worst mode. eps_op *is* the worst-case relative compliance error over all loads, not merely a bound. The measured 0.31% at eps_op 0.152 [ASSEMBLY / DELIVERABLE] is favourable alignment (58x below the sharp bound); a TO run that explores loads and designs will eventually excite thin-region bending and see numbers closer to eps_op.
* **Exact composition.** Loewner order is preserved by congruence and sums: if each cell satisfies the sandwich with eps, the lattice K = sum P_c^T S_c P_c satisfies (1-eps) K <= Khat <= (1+eps) K for any lattice, any boundary conditions, any load. Then C/(1+eps) <= Chat <= C/(1-eps) and ||uhat - u||_K <= eps/(1-eps) ||u||_K (from uhat - u = Khat^{-1}(K - Khat) u and ||M^{-1}(I-M)|| = max|1-mu|/mu). Element sensitivities s_e = -u^T K'_e u obey |shat_e - s_e| <= ||uhat-u||_{K'_e} ||uhat+u||_{K'_e}, controlled in absolute terms relative to total energy. The module certificate is the lattice certificate. The Schur complement is also monotone and homogeneous, so d_T is non-expansive under condensation as well: if the *full* (interior + trace) stiffness satisfies the sandwich with delta, so does S.
* **Additive vs multiplicative.** Ahat = A + E: |mu-1| <= ||E||_2 / lam_min, so +-3% needs ||E||_2 <= 1.46e-8 = 4.2e-7 relative [METRIC]. Rhat = (I+Delta) R*: M = (I+Delta)^T (I+Delta), eps_op <= 2||Delta|| + ||Delta||^2 with no reference to A (measured ~1.42||Delta|| for random Delta, the sqrt(2) of adding Delta and Delta^T incoherently) [METRIC]. Two further cases the project has not stated: Rhat = R*(I+Delta) (right-multiplicative, column-space error) is conjugated by R*, amplified by cond(R*) = sqrt(cond A) = 269; an additive factor error F gives Delta = F R*^{-1}, ||Delta|| <= ||F||/sqrt(lam_min) = (||F||/||R*||) sqrt(cond A): additive errors on the factor are amplified by 269, on A by 7.2e4. Column scaling by predicted compliances 1/sqrt((A^{-1})_jj) [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (b)] is the diagonal approximation of the right whitening, which is why it reduced the curvature spread from 1e4 to 16.8 and why Newton (affine invariant) converged where Adam in raw coordinates diverged.
* **Per-element relative errors are not amplified.** If Khat_e is Loewner-within delta_e of K_e for every element (or coarse cell, or GP face), the assembled full stiffness is within max delta_e and therefore so is S. This is the single most consequential fact for the design: a representation built from local SPD contributions with *relative* parameter errors needs those errors to be ~3%, not 1e-4.

### 2.2 Why averaged losses cannot see the deciding modes

Any average L = (1/d) sum phi(mu_i) with phi(mu) ~ (mu-1)^2/2 near 1 satisfies max|mu-1| <= sqrt(2 d L) and nothing better. At d = 12,792, L = D/d = 1.27e-5 permits eps_op up to 0.57; the measured 0.229 with 3 deciding modes is exactly this gap [METRIC]. Frobenius on A weights mode i by lam_i^2, so a soft mode's O(1) error carries weight (lam_min/lam_max)^2 = 2e-10; action-MSE with random probes is the same weighting; the whitened Frobenius ||M-I||_F^2 = sum (mu_i-1)^2 weights modes equally but still cannot distinguish 3 modes at 0.23 from all modes at 0.004 in its *value* (its gradient does push on the bad modes proportionally, so it is a fine bulk term for optimisation, not a certificate). The "+-3% necessary line" D/d <= phi(0.97) = 4.59e-4 is necessary only.

### 2.3 What a loss must look like to control max|mu-1|

The loss must dominate max|mu-1| with a d-independent constant. Options, all functions of Ahat's action only (gauge invariance):

1. **Extreme-mode terms.** lambda_max(M) and lambda_min(M) via the Rayleigh quotients x^T Ahat x / x^T A x at the extremal directions; the (sub)gradient of lambda_max w.r.t. parameters is the derivative of that Rayleigh quotient at the current extremal vector, one operator apply. Use *both* ends and a soft-max (log-sum-exp with temperature beta, error log(k)/beta) over the k worst Ritz values on each side; one-sided extreme terms produce the measured whack-a-mole (mu_max 15 -> 5, mu_min 0.13 -> 0.05) [LEARNING ATTEMPTS]. The symmetric per-mode function |log mu| is preferable to |mu-1| (inversion-symmetric).
2. **Schatten-2k moments.** tr((M-I)^{2k})^{1/2k} >= ||M-I||_2 and <= d^{1/2k} ||M-I||_2 (1.34 for 2k = 32): a certified upper bound on eps_op computable by Hutchinson probes, tr X^{2k} = E ||X^k z||^2, with 2k applies per probe. Smooth, two-sided, d-almost-independent.
3. **Loewner barrier.** B_eps(M) = -sum_i [log(1+eps-mu_i) + log(mu_i-(1-eps))], self-concordant, infinite at the gate walls, minimised at mu = 1; gradient via tr(X^{-1} dX) (Hutchinson + CG). Requires a feasible start, so run an eps-homotopy (interior-point path following) from eps_0 = current eps_op + margin down to 0.03. The divergence D = tr M - log det M - d is the one-sided eps -> infinity limit of this family, which is why it under-weights the outliers.

In all cases pair the tail term with a well-conditioned bulk term (whitened divergence or sum (log mu_i)^2) so the bulk keeps converging while the tail is pinned.

### 2.4 Estimating max|mu-1| cheaply during training

On teacher seats whitening is exact and cheap: one apply of M costs one apply of Ahat plus two dense triangular solves with R* (1.6e8 flops each at d = 12.8k). Lanczos converges fastest exactly for isolated outliers, and the deciding modes are isolated (3 of 12,792) and drift slowly across steps, so: warm-started block Lanczos/LOBPCG with 8-32 vectors and 2-5 iterations per step, a full restart every ~100 steps to catch new outliers, fixed probes from the teacher's precomputed softest eigenvectors (a lower bound at zero cost), a Schatten-2k Hutchinson estimate as an upper bound, and an exact eigendecomposition (d^3 ~ 2e12 flops, tens of seconds on a GPU) per epoch as the audit. The whole tail machinery costs ~100 operator applies per step. For the largest seats (q ~ 48k) scale accordingly; it remains far below the teacher's 31.85 s.

## 3. Uniqueness and gauge

**Cholesky.** For a fixed ordering, A -> R (positive diagonal) is unique and real-analytic on the SPD cone. Its derivative in the whitened metric is Z = dR R^{-1} = Phi(W) with W = R^{-T} dA R^{-1} and Phi = upper-triangular part with half diagonal; ||Phi(W)||_F <= ||W||_F and ||Phi(W)||_2 <= (log d / pi + O(1)) ||W||_2 ~ 3 ||W||_2. So the factor is as continuous in geometry as A itself (in the right metric), and the ordering must be geometry-independent: use the background-grid superset ordering with inactive dofs masked. Caveat: the trace dof *set* varies with geometry, and the Cholesky factor of a principal submatrix is not a sub-block of the factor, so dense-factor labels are different objects across geometries; and each entry of R* is a product of a sequential elimination, i.e. a *global* function of geometry even though its sparsity structure is local. That makes factor entries poor regression targets even though they are unique.

**SVD / low-rank factors.** U Sigma V^T is unique only up to signs and rotations within (near-)degenerate singular subspaces; the sensitivity of a singular vector is ~1/(sigma_k - sigma_{k+1}), unbounded. Factor coefficients are therefore discontinuous labels while the rank-r product is well conditioned. Canonical, continuous alternatives exist and should be used if a hierarchical representation is learned: (i) fixed-probe sketches Y = B Omega with a fixed Omega (linear in B) and Q = qr_+(Y) (positive-diagonal QR, smooth where Y has full rank), or the symmetric/generalised Nystrom data (B Omega, Psi^T B, Psi^T B Omega), all *linear* functionals of the operator; (ii) fixed-skeleton CUR/interpolative decompositions, where the factor B[:, J] is a sub-block of the operator itself. Both make the block data a gauge-free, continuous, and directly supervisable (from S packets) target; Nystrom-type reconstruction amplifies data errors by ~sigma_1/sigma_r, which bounds how far ranks may be pushed.

**T^T D T and auxiliaries.** (T, D) -> (G T, G^{-T} D G^{-1}) for any structure-preserving G leaves the operator unchanged; likewise the M/U auxiliaries of the old backend. A loss that is not a pure function of the operator will drift along the gauge orbit, which is what the 2.5x distortion was [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (c)]. Rule: the loss is a function of Ahat's action only, and the parameterisation's gauge group is trivial (positive diagonal + triangularity, fixed probes, fixed local bases, positive weights). Even with action supervision, a free gauge lets different seats settle in different gauges and destroys generalisation across geometries, so the gauge must be fixed in the parameterisation, not only quotiented in the loss.

**Coefficients vs action.** Coefficient regression ||c - c*|| needs a canonical c* and measures error in the coefficient metric, which maps to d_T through the Jacobian of c -> Ahat with condition number up to cond(A) (additive), sqrt(cond) (factor-additive) or ~1 (multiplicative/whitened). Supervising the action with the whitened loss is always at least as good and is exact on the seats; the only price is that gradients flow through the reconstruction.

## 4. Per-entry accuracy: analytic derivation and reconciliation

Let Rhat = R* + F, Delta = F R*^{-1}, eps_op ~ 2||Delta||_2 to first order.

**Independent entry-relative noise** F_ij = eps xi_ij R*_ij, xi iid N(0,1). For any unit w, E||F w||^2 = eps^2 sum_j (sum_i R*_ij^2) w_j^2 = eps^2 w^T diag(A) w exactly (column j of R* has squared norm A_jj). Take w the softest eigenvector and y = R* w / sqrt(lam_min) (unit): Delta y = F w / sqrt(lam_min), hence

||Delta||_2 >= eps sqrt(w^T diag(A) w / w^T A w) = eps sqrt(rho_J(w)),   eps_op ~ 2 eps sqrt(rho_J).

With rho_J = 1e3-1e4 [STRUCTURE OF S] this predicts eps_op/eps in 63-200; measured 111 (1.11e-2 at eps = 1e-4) [ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS], i.e. rho_J,eff ~ 3e3. The matching upper bound uses ||F||_2 <~ eps (max_j sqrt(A_jj) + max_i ||R*_{i,:}||) (Latala; Bandeira-van Handel) and ||R*^{-1}|| = 1/sqrt(lam_min): eps_op <~ 2 eps sqrt(max_j A_jj / lam_min) ~ 2 * 269 eps = 5.4e-2 at 1e-4. The measurement sits between the mode-weighted and the worst-case Jacobi ratio, as it must. For iid *absolute* noise sigma the same argument gives eps_op ~ 2 sigma sqrt(d/lam_min): the random-matrix sqrt(d) is real, and it is replaced for relative noise by the effective count sqrt(w^T diag(A) w)/eps-scale of entries that matter.

**Predicting A instead.** E = eps Xi o A: var(w^T E w) = eps^2 sum_ij A_ij^2 w_i^2 w_j^2 <= eps^2 (w^T diag(A) w)^2 by A_ij^2 <= A_ii A_jj, so eps_op <~ eps rho_J against 2 eps sqrt(rho_J) for the factor. Measured 545 eps vs 111 eps (5x) [ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS]: between sqrt(rho_J) and rho_J because the Cauchy-Schwarz step is loose. The factor is the better target in every noise model.

**Coherent (block-constant) relative errors.** E||F w||^2 = eps^2 sum_i sum_B (sum_{j in B} R*_ij w_j)^2, which exceeds the independent value by at most n_B (Cauchy-Schwarz), with equality only if R*_ij w_j has constant sign inside blocks. Measured ratio (2.43e-2/1.12e-2)^2 ~ 4.7 at n_B = 512 [ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS]: the factor's rows oscillate in sign (a half-order operator), so block coherence buys little. In the fully coherent limit (one global relative offset) F = eps xi R* is a pure scaling and eps_op = 2 eps |xi| with *no* amplification: coherence is non-monotone in correlation length; what matters is the *shape* of the error relative to the cancellation.

**The missing noise model, and the one that matters.** A relative bias delta between the near-field and far-field parts of R* (or of S) changes the soft mode's stiffness by ~delta rho_J lam_soft: eps_op ~ delta rho_J, so +-3% needs delta <= 3e-6..3e-5. Banding is the extreme case delta = 1 and gives eps_op ~ rho_R, the measured 59-144. This is the natural failure mode of any predictor that emits near and far field through different parameters or heads, and of any truncation scheme; it is captured by neither the independent nor the block-constant test. The old backend's tensor-RMS 1e-3 perturbation moving the spectrum to [0.707, 1.377] is a different phenomenon: the parameter-to-operator Jacobian of that parameterisation had top singular values ~300x its rms (the measured curvature spread), a property of the parameterisation, cured by whitening the parameterisation.

**Rank-dependent accuracy.** Because soft modes are smooth, the leading (smooth) singular components of far-field blocks must be coherent with the near field to ~1e-5 relative, while the high-rank tails may be loose by 1e-2. Any learned hierarchical model should allocate precision that way; and this is the quantitative reason SVD-truncated H-matrices pass at block tolerances far looser than 1e-4.

## 5. Required smoothness of geometry -> S

### 5.1 The exact structure of the teacher's map

Q2 shape-function gradients are polynomials of degree <= 2 per variable, so every cut-cell element matrix is *linear* in the 125 monomial moments m_alpha = integral_{cell ∩ Omega} x^alpha (alpha_k <= 4) of the material region: K_e = sum_alpha m_alpha^e G_alpha with constant matrices G_alpha. Ghost-penalty face matrices are integrals over whole background faces and are geometry-independent constants J_F; only the face *set* GP(theta) depends on geometry. Hence

A_full(theta) = sum_e sum_alpha m_alpha^e(theta) G_alpha + gamma sum_{F in GP(theta)} J_F,

and S(theta) is a rational function of the moments between events. The moments are C^1 in the level-set coefficients (kinks in the second derivative when the surface crosses a background vertex or edge). The only genuine discontinuities are the switches of GP(theta) (and of the active dof set, which is continuous if inactive dofs are extended by zero). A switch adds gamma J_F, tiny in absolute terms, but the soft modes have stiffness ~1e-6, so the relative effect is O(1): a +0.01% thickness change activated a 5.6e-15 volume-fraction cell with 3 new GP faces and stiffened one 1.1e-6 direction by 59.8% [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY OF THE TEACHER]. The mechanism is GP bridging: a nearly empty cell with faces to several neighbours couples their extended polynomials at stiffness ~gamma, comparable to the physical stiffness of a thin region. Between events the whitened Lipschitz constant is benign, O(1-3) per unit *relative* thickness (bending ~t^3), which is why end-load compliance derivatives agree to 0.023% while operator central differences disagree by 87%: the stencil straddles events that end loads do not excite. The cross-seat eps_op 536-3847 is consistent with smooth t^3 physics applied to thin regions whose local thickness differs by an order of magnitude between seats; it is a statement about the metric's sensitivity to log-thickness of the thinnest material, not about intrinsic roughness.

### 5.2 What regularity is needed, and what is available

For a target that is only Lipschitz on a p-dimensional parameter box, worst-case n-sample rates are n^{-1/p}-type; for C^k, n^{-k/p}; for analytic, exp(-c n^{1/p}). With p ~ 9 (8 corner thicknesses + cut plane) and n = 33 x 48 or 1024 x 48 samples, n^{1/9} ~ 2-3 points per axis: *no* smoothness class makes a global map theta -> S learnable to 1e-4 coherence, and against the current teacher the map is not even continuous on the deciding modes. Generalisation must come from compositional locality: theta -> (local geometry per cell, a ~6-8 dimensional smooth quantity) -> (local SPD contributions) -> (exact global algebra). The first two are learnable (or computable) from 1e5-1e7 local samples; the third needs no data.

### 5.3 If the map is only piecewise smooth

* **Smooth the teacher (recommended).** Replace the hard cell classification by a continuous aggregation/ghost weight w(alpha) that is a smooth function of the cut fraction alpha, tending to a hard constraint (AgFEM limit) as alpha -> 0 and vanishing as alpha -> 1. Then a cell's contribution vanishes continuously as it empties, S(theta) becomes continuous and piecewise analytic with C^0 kinks at vertex-crossing events, and the 1e-12 threshold sensitivity of the internal-extension prototype [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY OF THE TEACHER] disappears by construction. Randomised smoothing (averaging the teacher over jittered thresholds, an average of SPD matrices sandwiched by the family's min and max) is a fallback that costs several teacher runs per label. Regenerating 33 seats and the 1024 batch is hours on 64 cores [TOOLS AVAILABLE].
* **Register a spectral floor.** Certify in the shifted metric (A + E, Ahat + E) with E a local PSD regulariser at the scale where GP bridging dominates physics (the spectrum evaluator already supports this). The shifted sandwich composes exactly (it is the certificate for the lattice with a known added regularising stiffness), and it is honest: the Tet10 validation probed end-load compliance, which is insensitive to gamma (0.01-0.04% for halving/doubling), never the 1e-6 modes.
* **Add active-set features.** Volume fractions, GP indicators and node masks are exact inputs at inference and should always be given; but they only make the discontinuity representable for *local* outputs. A global output (factor entries, H-blocks) would have to route a 1e-15-thin local switch into a 60% change of a global mode, which no smooth network trained on 1e3 geometries will do.
* **Accept and localise.** With a Schur-structured representation the jump is produced by exact algebra from the switched local terms; it costs nothing. With a global regression it is unlearnable.

## 6. Sample complexity and the data at hand

* **Global route.** 33 factors, 1024 S packets, 48 symmetries: ~5e4 global samples, ~3 per geometry axis. The stiff bulk of S may be nearly additive in the corner thicknesses and could be captured to ~10% (the V1 CNN underfit at 27% because its representation class provably could not pass and its receptive radius 0.23 was local while its outputs were global [LEARNING ATTEMPTS]); the deciding modes need near/far coherence at 3e-6..3e-5 and cannot be interpolated from this many points.
* **Local route.** Objects that are local functions of geometry (element matrices, GP faces, locally upscaled coarse tensors) are exactly weight-shareable: 33 x 7,478 cut cells ~ 2.5e5 samples (1.2e7 with symmetries, or equivalently a 48x smaller equivariant network), 33 x 1096 coarse cells ~ 3.6e4. A smooth map of ~6-8 effective inputs at these sample sizes reaches 1e-3-1e-4 (kernel-rate estimate n^{-k/(k+p)} with k ~ 4), and the per-element *relative* tolerance is 3%, not 1e-4 (section 2.1). Entries or blocks of S/R* are not local functions of geometry (the interior solve enters), so weight sharing on them is a biased estimator with bias exactly in the deciding modes. The dof-compliance predictor (R^2 0.98 locally) shows that some global quantities are locally predictable to ~10%, which is useful for whitening, not for accuracy.
* **Use all 1024 packets.** A dense Cholesky of a q ~ 1.3e4 packet is d^3/3 ~ 7e11 flops (seconds on a GPU; ~1 minute for the largest q ~ 4.8e4), far below the 31.85 s teacher: the "only 33 have factors" constraint is removable in an afternoon, giving whitened labels for all 1024 geometries.
* **Which seats.** The seats sparsely sample geometry, and the Thompson-distance between them is huge; for a local-route model that is irrelevant (each seat supplies thousands of local samples); for a global-route model it means the training set does not cover the soft-mode structure of unseen geometries at all.

## 7. Recommendation: cleanest target and cleanest certificate

**Target (Tier A).** Regress, or better compute, *local SPD contributions in fixed local bases*: cut-cell moments (hence element matrices, linear in them), the GP face set, and, if a reduced core is used, local core tensors or a locally computed enrichment (GenEO/MsFEM-type local eigenmodes). Generate the operator by exact algebra: assembly + Schur complement on a reduced interior (one fine collar layer + a core with shell-like or spectrally enriched kinematics; ~1e4-6e4 dofs; seconds). Parameterise every learned quantity multiplicatively (positive weights, log-scales, SPD tensors) so that relative parameter errors are relative Loewner errors and eps_op <= max local error, with the bulk of the certificate coming from Shat >= S (Galerkin) and the Loewner composition (1-delta) S <= Shat <= (1+delta)(1+eta) S, delta = worst local relative error, eta = core excess. This is the representation in which the near/far cancellation, the rigid nullspace, SPD-ness, the GP-event discontinuity, weight sharing, cube-group equivariance and the +-3% tolerance per parameter all come for free, and it is the only one for which the measurements (23k parameters -> eps_op 0.15, vs 7.4M -> 15.2) do not contradict theory. Its cost target is the reduced condensation plus fast moment quadrature; the current 30 s is assembly code, not mathematics.

**Target (Tier B, if an interior solve at inference is forbidden).** An H^2/FMM-shaped equivariant network on a fixed background cluster tree whose outputs are gauge-free block data (dense near-field blocks, fixed-probe sketches of admissible blocks with fixed ranks per level), supervised on the operator's action with a whitened bulk + two-sided tail loss on all 1024 factored packets, outputs pre-whitened by predicted compliances. Expectation from the analysis: the +-10% work gate on the bulk is plausible, the deciding modes are not, because near/far coherence at 3e-6..3e-5 must be inferred from ~3 samples per geometry axis. Run the decisive oracle first: perturb the passing H-matrix's near and far fields by independent smooth relative fields at 1e-3 and 1e-4 and read eps_op.

**Certificate.** Per module, d_T(S, Shat) = max(log mu_max, -log mu_min), reported with eps_op, the count of modes outside +-3% and +-10%, and the soft-subspace projection of the residual; computed by Lanczos on the whitened pencil on teacher seats (exact audit by eigendecomposition). It composes to the lattice for every load and design, gives Chat/C in [1/(1+eps), 1/(1-eps)] and energy-norm displacement error eps/(1-eps), and is sharp. If the teacher's GP-dominated modes are not physically validated, register the shifted metric (A+E) as the contract. For derivatives, a uniform sandwich over a theta-ball of radius h yields a whitened bound ~2 eps ||S||/h on the operator derivative error; for TO, prefer a task-level derivative certificate with a registered load scope, since the operator derivative of the current teacher does not exist. For new geometries without a teacher, the only teacher-free certificates are structural one-sided bounds (Galerkin Shat >= S; Nystrom-type Ahat <= A) and hypercircle-type a posteriori bounds that require fine element matrices (cheap) but not the fine condensation (expensive); spot-check certification with the teacher costs one teacher run.

**On the open decisions [OPEN DECISIONS FOR THE USER].** (1) Keep the module-level Loewner contract (it composes and is sharp) but register a spectral floor if the softest modes are GP artefacts. (2) Mode A with a Schur-structured representation; mode B only relaxes the gate to d_T <~ log 1.3 while reintroducing fine interior solves per lattice solve. (3) A reduced interior solve of seconds per cell is, by the analysis of section 1, the price of coherence; without it a +-3% certificate on the deciding modes is not expected. (4) Yes: regenerate labels with a continuous stabilisation; the current teacher's map is discontinuous exactly on the modes that decide the verdict.
